newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-PERU STAY IN FIGHT FOR WORLD CUP PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PERU STAY IN FIGHT FOR WORLD CUP PLACE.

text.p: Peru beat Bolivia 2-1 Sunday to keep themselves in the fight for a place at next year's World Cup while severely denting the prospects of their beaten neighbours at the same time.
Peru moved into fifth place in the South American qualifying group, level on 16 points with Chile, while Bolivia stayed seventh, two points behind the two Pacific countries and one behind Ecuador.
German Carty opened the scoring after 10 minutes when he provided the finishing touch to a superb run and cross by full-back Percy Olivares, who left two defenders in his wake.
Carty also set up the second goal in the 51st minute, providing the cross from which Jose Soto headed the ball into the net.

Bolivia, beaten in the final of the Copa America by Brazil last Sunday, got back into the game three minutes later when Luis Cristaldo scored, although Peru claimed he used his hand to control the ball.
Defender Marco Sandy missed a good chance to equalise for the Copa America hosts when he headed wide from an excellent position midway through the second half.
"We didn't deserve to lose this game," said their Spanish coach Antonio Lopez.

Bolivia, who had captain Vladimir Soria sent off in the second half of a rough game, look increasingly unlikely to reach their second successive World Cup as they have only one of their last five games at home.
Peru, despite their win, still have a lot of work to do to as they have played a game more than Chile and have a worse goal difference. The top four teams in the group qualify for France next year.
